tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__dc2c4692-a6c6-4edb-8301-12e868909281__firecrawl_scrape
tools.description: Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call. Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

schema.description: Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call. Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

tools.name: mcp__dc2c4692-a6c6-4edb-8301-12e868909281__firecrawl_search
tools.description: Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`. For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. # Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## Local Chrome

The default daemon can keep many tabs and visit many sites; browser-use has
no per-site, screenshot, or result-count limit that requires a new daemon.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination

## OCR (Tesseract Fallback)

Google Vision is not configured. Tesseract will be used for OCR but works poorly
on handwriting. For better results, either:
- Configure GOOGLE_VISION_API_KEY for Google Vision
- Set REMARKABLE_OCR_BACKEND=sampling to use this client's AI for OCR

# skills/CLAUDE.md

Local conventions for skill work in this repo. The authoring method itself lives
in one place: **`anthropic-skills:skill-creator`** (drafting, evals, trigger tests,
description optimization). For prose style, `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`
is the companion reference. Use your judgement on everything else.

(CreateSkill, a LifeOS fork with 17 broken pointers, was deleted 2026-09-22.
Recover it from git history if ever needed.)

## Owned vs vendored

- This repo (`erash11/claude-skills`) is canonical and holds real directories only.
  `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.codex/skills` are generated views. Never author a skill there.
- A symlink here marks a third-party (vendored) skill: clone it to
  `~/.agents/skills/<name>` and link it into the harnesses. Don't rewrite vendored skills.
  Windows trap: plain `ln -s` silently copies. See memory note
  `project_third-party-skill-install.md`.
- After adding, renaming or removing a skill, run `sync-to-codex` with `DRY_RUN=1`
  first (Windows: `sync-to-codex.ps1`). If the skill should be routable, rebuild the
  router roster with `TypeSafe_Sandbox/skill_router/build_roster.py`.

## Worth keeping in every skill

- A `## Gotchas` section that collects lessons from real failures. Add to it after each miss.
- Descriptions say when to use the skill, and "Do not use for X (use Y)" when a
  neighbour is easily confused. Keep them under the 1024-char cap; enforcement text
  belongs in the body, not the description.
- Before committing, grep for personal or sensitive content: `eric_rash`,
  `kristinarash`, athlete names or IDs, `DexaProject` paths, and token or key values.
  When in doubt, keep the skill private.

## skill-creator on Windows

Its scripts assume macOS/Linux. Use the job's `tmp` dir instead of `/tmp`, skip
`open`/`nohup`, and render the eval viewer with `--static`. Python is on PATH (3.14).

content.content:
1	---
2	name: memory-write
3	description: >-
4	  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
5	  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
6	  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
7	  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
8	  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
9	  recall checks the injected snapshot, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
10	  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
11	---
12	
13	# Memory Write
14	
15	## Outcome
16	- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
17	- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
18	- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."
19	
20	## Pick the tier first
21	
22	Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"
23	
24	**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
25	- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
26	- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
27	- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
28	- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)
29	
30	**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
31	- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
32	- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
33	- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
34	- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`
35	
36	## Steps
37	
38	1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
39	2. **Read** the target file in full.
40	3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
41	4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
42	5. **Write** the change.
43	   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
44	   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
45	6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`
46	
47	## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug
48	
49	**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
50	already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
51	it in `name:` is the third copy.
52	
53	| File | `name:` |
54	|---|---|
55	| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
56	| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
57	| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
58	| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |
59	
60	Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
61	is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.
62	
63	`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.
64	
65	This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
66	corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
67	isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.
68	
69	## Actions
70	
71	- **add** — append (default)
72	- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
73	- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.
74	
75	## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
76	
77	When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.
78	
79	1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

Your `~/.claude` setup is already in good shape. I found one real error, two small cleanups, and four items that are your call. Nothing has been changed. The full write-up is in [prompt-audit-2026-10-19.md](prompt-audit-2026-10-19.md), with three ready-to-apply edits at the end.

- **The error: `memory-write` describes memory folder names wrongly.** It says only `/` and `.` become `-`, which can't produce any Windows folder name. `AGENTS.md` says every character that isn't a letter or digit becomes `-`. Your actual folders back `AGENTS.md`: `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` shows up as `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`. `AGENTS.md` also says `memory-write` wins when the two disagree, so the wrong rule is the one that applies. The edit fixes `memory-write` and leaves `AGENTS.md` alone.
- **`graphify` shouts its one instruction.** Line 214 stacks "MANDATORY", "MUST", "forbidden" and "you are doing this wrong". The edit keeps the instruction and its reason (subagents are 5-10x faster) and drops the volume. If you reinstall graphify from upstream, this edit will be lost.
- **`skills/CLAUDE.md` still carries a history note** about deleting CreateSkill on 2026-09-22. It states no rule and loads every time you work on skills, so the edit removes it.
- **Four items for you to decide:**
  - Many skills have dated lessons ("Seen 2026-09-04"). I kept them because `skills/CLAUDE.md` asks for these lessons and most of them explain a rule.
  - graphify requires spreading work across subagents, but `USER.md` says to use few subagents unless asked.
  - `impeccable` and `graphify` come from outside sources but are installed as normal folders, not links like your other outside skills.
  - Working memory says the Windows laptop runs no automation, but `claude-stack-doctor` lists a weekly scheduled task on it. One of them is out of date.

Most of the setup checked out. There are no outdated "think step by step" style instructions, no retired model names, and no rules banning formatting or progress updates. Every path your top-level files name still exists.

Two limits on what I checked:
- I didn't read the settings, hooks or credential files, since they can hold secrets.
- I didn't check skills that are links to outside copies or the archive folders, or read each skill's reference files line by line.

The app won't let a session use `~/.claude` as its folder because it's a protected location. So I read the files directly, and the report sits in a folder the app made for this session. It belongs in `~/.claude/audits/` next to the 2026-09-30 audit.

A startup check flagged one failure: on 2026-10-12, the job that saves each session into your daily memory log failed once because it hit its turn limit. A single failure like this is usually a passing problem. If it happens again, `/claude-stack-doctor` will show it.

If you want to keep this work, I can move this session to a folder you choose.

Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. # skills/CLAUDE.md

Local conventions for skill work in this repo. The authoring method itself lives
in one place: **`anthropic-skills:skill-creator`** (drafting, evals, trigger tests,
description optimization). For prose style, `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`
is the companion reference. Use your judgement on everything else.

(CreateSkill, a LifeOS fork with 17 broken pointers, was deleted 2026-09-22.
Recover it from git history if ever needed.)

## Owned vs vendored

- This repo (`erash11/claude-skills`) is canonical and holds real directories only.
  `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.codex/skills` are generated views. Never author a skill there.
- A symlink here marks a third-party (vendored) skill: clone it to
  `~/.agents/skills/<name>` and link it into the harnesses. Don't rewrite vendored skills.
  Windows trap: plain `ln -s` silently copies. See memory note
  `project_third-party-skill-install.md`.
- After adding, renaming or removing a skill, run `sync-to-codex` with `DRY_RUN=1`
  first (Windows: `sync-to-codex.ps1`). If the skill should be routable, rebuild the
  router roster with `TypeSafe_Sandbox/skill_router/build_roster.py`.

## Worth keeping in every skill

- A `## Gotchas` section that collects lessons from real failures. Add to it after each miss.
- Descriptions say when to use the skill, and "Do not use for X (use Y)" when a
  neighbour is easily confused. Keep them under the 1024-char cap; enforcement text
  belongs in the body, not the description.
- Before committing, grep for personal or sensitive content: `eric_rash`,
  `kristinarash`, athlete names or IDs, `DexaProject` paths, and token or key values.
  When in doubt, keep the skill private.

## skill-creator on Windows

Its scripts assume macOS/Linux. Use the job's `tmp` dir instead of `/tmp`, skip
`open`/`nohup`, and render the eval viewer with `--static`. Python is on PATH (3.14).

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- **Deliverables.** A finished file made for someone else this session (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a copy at `~/DEV/_DRIVE/03_REPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>`. The repo keeps the source; Drive keeps the handed-off copy. Name the copy in the report.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.

# 2026-10-19 — Prompt audit of ~/.claude (Windows)

## What and why
Ran `/claude-api prompt-audit` over the user-level Claude Code setup (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md,
machine.md, skills/CLAUDE.md, 38 live skills, 4 agents), checked against claude-opus-5-5. The goal
was to find instructions written for older models, plus files that contradict each other or the repo.

## Result
- Group 1 (dated prompt text) was nearly clean: no thinking scaffolds, no retired model names, no
  update suppressors. Only one passage shouted without a reason (graphify).
- One real error: `memory-write` described slugs as "/ and . become -", which contradicts AGENTS.md
  and the actual slug folders (every non-alphanumeric character becomes "-").
- Full report: `~/.claude/audits/2026-10-19-prompt-audit.md`.

## Changes (claude-skills `6213750`, pushed)
- `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — slug rule matches AGENTS.md.
- `~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` — Agent-tool line stated plainly with its reason.
- `~/.claude/skills/CLAUDE.md` — CreateSkill deletion note removed.
- Views re-synced with `sync-to-codex.ps1` (44 entries to `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.codex/skills`).

## Other state changes
- `~/.claude` (dotclaude) was 55 commits behind and could not fast-forward. Stashed `settings.json`,
  restored 209 transcript files removed by Claude Code's auto-cleanup (all in commit `d16bf58`),
  pulled, then popped the stash. Settings merged cleanly: Mac's `opus[1m]` default, modelSettings and
  session-autopush hook, plus the local plugin toggles (playwright, commit-commands, github,
  claude-mem-cowork). Live `projects/` transcripts left uncommitted, per the 2026-10-16 STATUS rule.

- G-2: graphify requires subagent fan-out; USER.md says few subagents unless asked. Is `/graphify` an exception?
- G-3: impeccable and graphify are upstream skills installed as real folders; skills/CLAUDE.md says vendored skills are symlinks. Symlink them, or list them as exceptions?
- G-4: MEMORY.md says the Windows laptop has no automation since 10/8, but claude-stack-doctor lists `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` as active. Which is current?
- The GitHub plugin is enabled but its MCP server returned 401 this session (token rejected).

## Next
1. On the Mac: `git -C ~/.claude/skills pull`, then `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh`.

## Gotchas
- **A hand-run `memsearch index` takes no lock.** Only the SessionEnd hook and daily-backup use `.memsearch-index.lock`, so a manual rebuild collides with the next backup and Milvus Lite reports it as "older database". Write the rebuild's PID into the lock, or start it through the hook (2026-10-11).
- **`.errors.log` syncs between machines.** A Windows failure shows up on the Mac. Look for
  `C:\Users\` in a traceback before debugging on the wrong machine (2026-10-07).
- **dcg self-heal rewrites settings.json.** With `self_heal_hook = true` (the default) every dcg run re-adds the absolute-path hook. Keep it `false` in `~/.config/dcg/config.toml`; a dcg update may reset it (2026-10-11).

  re-adds a Mac-only line that then gets swept into a settings commit (e72c374).

  plus three named config repos, so `claude-memory-compiler` sat on an unmerged branch for 17
  days while closeout reported "clear to sign off". A sweep must walk nested git repos under
  `~/.claude` too, and should flag any repo not on `main`/`master`, not just dirty ones.
- A pre-merge `git merge-tree` "clean" result is not trustworthy - it reported clean for a merge
  that then conflicted on `uv.lock`. Merge into the feature branch first and look.
- `projects/**.jsonl` files are live session logs and may change again after a closeout commit when the stop hook writes its final entry.
- `scripts/backup-manifest.json` is **not** globally sorted — some `DEV/` entries were appended
  after the non-`DEV` block. Insert new entries in place; a full re-sort churns unrelated lines.
  `json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"` round-trips the file byte-identically.
- Two sessions can write to this repo at once. Check `git log` before assuming a change is yours.
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents` is **not backed up** - not in `backup-manifest.json`, not snapshotted.
  The launchd job definitions exist in exactly one place on this machine.
- After editing a launchd plist, reload it or the change does nothing:
  `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label>` then `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) <plist>`.
  Confirm with `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/<label>`.
- `daily-backup.out` now grows with every run, as `daily-backup.log` already did. Neither is
  rotated.
- **There is no "no-op push" bug, despite the 2026-09-17 note saying so.** A genuine no-op push
  prints `Everything up-to-date` to stderr and exits **0**, and the script only records an error
  on a non-zero exit, so it stays silent. Verified on a throwaway repo 2026-09-19.
  The 2026-09-17 `repo-push:dotclaude` error was a REAL failure - the full block reads
  `RPC failed; curl 55 Recv failure`, `send-pack: unexpected disconnect`,
  `fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly`, and `Everything up-to-date` was merely the last
  of git's four stderr lines. Reading one line out of four produced the wrong diagnosis, and the
  double-logging made that block twice as long and easy to misread.
- That 2026-09-17 failure was a transient network error, and the job has **no retry**. A push
  that fails this way is not reattempted until the next day's run.

## Gotchas
- **A hand-run `memsearch index` takes no lock.** Only the SessionEnd hook and daily-backup use `.memsearch-index.lock`, so a manual rebuild collides with the next backup and Milvus Lite reports it as "older database". Write the rebuild's PID into the lock, or start it through the hook (2026-10-11).
- **`.errors.log` syncs between machines.** A Windows failure shows up on the Mac. Look for
  `C:\Users\` in a traceback before debugging on the wrong machine (2026-10-07).
- **dcg self-heal rewrites settings.json.** With `self_heal_hook = true` (the default) every dcg run re-adds the absolute-path hook. Keep it `false` in `~/.config/dcg/config.toml`; a dcg update may reset it (2026-10-11).
- **Never run `dcg install` here.** `dcg doctor` only recognizes the absolute-path hook and
  will ask for it; the portable guarded entry already covers both machines. Installing
  re-adds a Mac-only line that then gets swept into a settings commit (e72c374).
- **The closeout repo sweep used to miss nested repos under `~/.claude`.** It walked `~/DEV`
  plus three named config repos, so `claude-memory-compiler` sat on an unmerged branch for 17
  days while closeout reported "clear to sign off". A sweep must walk nested git repos under
  `~/.claude` too, and should flag any repo not on `main`/`master`, not just dirty ones.
- A pre-merge `git merge-tree` "clean" result is not trustworthy - it reported clean for a merge
  that then conflicted on `uv.lock`. Merge into the feature branch first and look.
- `projects/**.jsonl` files are live session logs and may change again after a closeout commit when the stop hook writes its final entry.
- `scripts/backup-manifest.json` is **not** globally sorted — some `DEV/` entries were appended
  after the non-`DEV` block. Insert new entries in place; a full re-sort churns unrelated lines.
  `json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"` round-trips the file byte-identically.
- Two sessions can write to this repo at once. Check `git log` before assuming a change is yours.
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents` is **not backed up** - not in `backup-manifest.json`, not snapshotted.
  The launchd job definitions exist in exactly one place on this machine.
- After editing a launchd plist, reload it or the change does nothing:
  `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label>` then `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) <plist>`.
  Confirm with `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/<label>`.
- `daily-backup.out` now grows with every run, as `daily-backup.log` already did. Neither is
  rotated.
- **There is no "no-op push" bug, despite the 2026-09-17 note saying so.** A genuine no-op push
  prints `Everything up-to-date` to stderr and exits **0**, and the script only records an error
  on a non-zero exit, so it stays silent. Verified on a throwaway repo 2026-09-19.
  The 2026-09-17 `repo-push:dotclaude` error was a REAL failure - the full block reads
  `RPC failed; curl 55 Recv failure`, `send-pack: unexpected disconnect`,
  `fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly`, and `Everything up-to-date` was merely the last
  of git's four stderr lines. Reading one line out of four produced the wrong diagnosis, and the
  double-logging made that block twice as long and easy to misread.
- That 2026-09-17 failure was a transient network error, and the job has **no retry**. A push
  that fails this way is not reattempted until the next day's run.
